title: vision-agent-mcp
problem: An LLM agent needs computer-vision tools, and the quality of the tool descriptions decides how well it uses them.
built: An MCP server with five tools (list, detect, count, summarize and compare images) over a YOLOv8n ONNX detector, and a 36-case harness that scores the agent against COCO128 labels. Typed Python with 14 unit tests.
result: The agent scored 26/36 with the tools as first written. One sentence in two tool descriptions (retry once at lower confidence) lifted it to 28/36. The detector alone scored 26/36.
limits: 36 cases and one run per setting, so the gain is a signal and not proof. The detector was trained on COCO images, so absolute numbers are optimistic. The README lists two evaluation flaws found and fixed.

title: Multi-agent engineering workflow
problem: Several projects run at the same time and one person cannot supervise every task by hand.
built: A daily workflow with leads, workers, supervision and decision routing, used to deliver across the projects on this page.
result: Used every working day on real delivery.
limits: Internal tooling. It has no public repository and no benchmark.
headline: daily use

title: HelperBot
problem: Play KeyForge, a game with hidden information, a large action space and no clean search tree.
built: An AlphaZero-style self-play agent (MCTS plus a learned policy and value network) that plays through the open-source keyteki engine. Hexagonal layers across Python training and Node.js inference. 13 architecture decision records, a PRD and the full task tree are committed with the code.
result: Training and inference run end to end through the game engine.
limits: Independent project. No published win-rate benchmark.
headline: 13 ADRs

title: Real-time GPU vision pipeline
problem: Existing detection services were single-purpose and fragmented, and each new use case needed a new service.
built: Led the architecture of a next-generation pipeline: multi-stream decode, batched inference, concurrency model, service boundaries and an incremental migration path. Consolidated the services into one configurable inference layer behind a minimal shared contract. Tradeoffs are recorded as architecture decision records.
result: A lean edge camera runtime measured about 31 MB of extra memory per additional FHD camera against a 250 MB budget, with a design target of at least 9 concurrent FHD cameras per x86_64 host.
limits: Company work. Numbers are from design and measurement on the team's own hardware.
headline: ~31 MB per camera

title: PPE detection for drilling operations
problem: Rig operations need automatic monitoring of personal protective equipment.
built: Fine-tuned detection models on annotated drill-floor data and wired alert emission into the platform. Added LLM-based validation of safety-equipment alerts.
result: LLM validation cut false positives by over 95%, at the cost of one Gemini inference per alert.
limits: Company work. Client details are not published.
headline: -95% false alerts

title: Oil-spill crisis-management platform
problem: Offshore clients need to see spill boundaries and nearby vessels, people and fauna to coordinate a response.
built: An end-to-end platform: instance segmentation for spill boundaries, object detection for vessels, people and fauna, and an operational coordination interface on AWS.
headline: end to end

title: Facial-expression effort model
problem: Estimate effort level in physical activity from facial expressions with little data.
built: A convolutional network with transfer learning, data augmentation and data cleaning (2022-2023).
result: Over 95% accuracy on low data with no overfitting.
limits: Small dataset. Not validated on new subjects.
headline: >95% accuracy

title: Electoral-analytics backend
problem: An analytics platform needed a backend over public electoral and census data.
built: The whole backend: a FastAPI service over BigQuery data, a PostgreSQL store with Alembic migrations, JWT authentication, rate limiting, transactional email, Docker and GCP deployment, and a test suite.
result: About 175 commits over four months as a freelance engineer.
limits: Client project. The code is private.
headline: ~175 commits

title: Contract-first Python services
problem: Services drift apart when their contracts live only in code.
built: Typed services built on AsyncAPI and JSON Schema contracts with generated Pydantic v2 models. A zone-evaluation library on hexagonal architecture, released next to its predecessor so consumers could migrate without a coordinated cutover.
result: Consumers migrated without a coordinated cutover.
headline: no cutover

title: People-analytics automation
problem: HCM data distribution took a week of manual work and access control had to meet LGPD.
built: Automated the distribution flow, built access-control applications for HCM data and attrition dashboards with sentiment analysis of free-text answers.
result: Distribution went from a week of manual work to immediate.
headline: 1 week → instant

title: Project Manager, maritime monitoring
problem: A vessel-based monitoring line needed a roadmap and delivery across onboard detection, a crew application and shore-side services.
built: Ran the roadmap and delivery. Delivered person and vessel detection with live inference on onboard video, and traced and fixed the model-format and GPU-memory defects that blocked it. Drove the bridge application work.

title: Railway false-alert analysis
problem: A railway obstruction monitor produced too many false alerts.
built: Analysed 67,000 alert thumbnails and showed that 21 of 119 camera scenes produced 92% of false alerts. Recommended a per-scene temporal model over the per-frame classifier. Managed the developers.
result: 92% of false alerts traced to 21 of 119 scenes.
limits: Company work. The recommendation is a design choice and was not proven in this analysis.
headline: 92% from 21 of 119 scenes

title: cv-label-audit
headline: 89% of injected label errors found
problem: Detection datasets carry label errors, and reviewing every image is slow.
built: A detector-based audit that flags missing boxes, wrong classes, loose boxes and unsupported boxes, stores findings in SQLite, and ranks images for review with one SQL query. Scored against errors injected with a fixed seed.
result: Recall 0.89 on auditable injected errors at the lowest threshold, precision 0.23. The top 10 review queue holds an injected error in 72% of images against 31% at random.
limits: COCO128 only. The detector saw these images in training, so recall is optimistic. Deleted boxes are found only 30% of the time. The audit was revised once after a first run raised too many flags.

title: cv-training-lab
headline: 90.4% test accuracy
problem: A training workflow needs architecture choice, tuning, versioning, explanation and monitoring, not only a model.
built: A reproducible CIFAR-10 pipeline: three architectures, random hyperparameter search, a file registry with checksums and promotion rules, Grad-CAM with a deletion test, and a drift monitor.
result: Test accuracy 0.706 (small CNN), 0.837 (ResNet-18 scratch), 0.904 (ResNet-18 pretrained). Search lifted the small CNN from 0.656 to 0.694. The drift monitor had no false alarms and flagged all four corruptions at 0.96 or above.
limits: One seed per row, 20,000 training images, one GPU. The Grad-CAM check is informative for the scratch model and not for the pretrained one. A first deletion test used an unfair baseline and was replaced.

title: lidar-camera-fusion
headline: 0.35 m vs 2.45 m error
problem: A camera alone gives a poor distance to detected objects.
built: LiDAR points projected into the image and fused with YOLOv8n detections to estimate object position, plus a nearest-neighbour tracker, scored against KITTI 3D tracklets.
result: Median distance error 0.35 m with fusion against 2.45 m camera only, and 92% of estimates within 10% against 50%.
limits: One KITTI drive of 108 frames. The tracker is weak (23 identity switches on 14 tracks). No radar, no 3D detector, no latency measurement.

title: edge-inference-bench
headline: 266 tok/s GPU, 78 CPU
problem: Running a language model locally needs known load time, memory and speed under real settings.
built: A C++17 harness over llama.cpp that measures load time, resident memory, prefill and decode speed, thread scaling, quantisation, load mode and long-session behaviour, on CPU and CUDA builds.
result: Decode speed stops scaling at 4 threads. Q8_0 decodes 12 to 15% slower than Q4_K_M. On the CPU, decode speed halves between 500 and 3,500 tokens of context. On the GPU it falls 7%.
limits: One 0.5 B model, one machine, warm page cache. No changes to llama.cpp itself and no Vulkan or Metal build.

title: ml-feature-serving
headline: AUC 0.72, not 0.94
problem: Models lose performance in production when serving features differ from training features.
built: One feature function shared by training and serving with an as-of rule, an online store, a scoring API that logs model and feature versions, population-stability drift checks, and Thompson-sampling traffic routing, on public credit data.
result: Leaky features lift AUC from 0.72 to 0.94. Offline and online features agree to 0.0. Routing cut regret from 260 to 18 over 5,000 replayed requests.
limits: Monthly data, SQLite instead of managed stores, replayed labels instead of live traffic. The drift monitor missed a 1.5 times shift and caught 2 times.

title: agent-retrieval-service
headline: nDCG@10 0.688
problem: An agent needs a retrieval tool that is measured, streamable and deployable.
built: BM25, dense and hybrid retrieval over SciFact, exposed as an MCP tool and a Server-Sent Events API, with a Dockerfile, a CI workflow and validated Terraform for Cloud Run.
result: Hybrid nDCG@10 0.688 against 0.666 for BM25 and 0.648 for dense. The BM25 score matches the published value.
limits: No language model in the loop. Terraform was validated and never applied. No authentication.
